requirements.requirement: curl package on node1 is version-locked at its current installed version (8.9.1-5.el10)
requirements.summary: Baseline curl version identified as 8.9.1-5.el10 (cmd-dcd886d4b2a5475e); dnf versionlock add curl applied (cmd-bdb20c5d62d64600) and confirmed present in both `dnf versionlock list` and /etc/dnf/plugins/versionlock.list (cmd-6ccaf47917914d07). The lock also survived the subsequent reboot (cmd-a3e47824ceaf43eb).

requirements.requirement: A system update leaves curl at its current (locked) version rather than upgrading it
requirements.summary: dnf check-update curl returned no curl update (cmd-90022c6ab7df4d70). A full `dnf update -y --assumeno` dry-run transaction that upgrades dozens of other packages (kernel, NetworkManager, dnf itself, etc., cmd-432cb9b712014d62) contains no entry for the curl package (grep for '^ curl ' returned no match, cmd-1b71f7b78dcc4253); only the separate libcurl sub-package appears, which is not the locked package. Post-reboot the installed curl version and versionlock entry are unchanged (cmd-a3e47824ceaf43eb).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — locking curl at its current version and demonstrating that a system update leaves it untouched — are directly and coherently evidenced. curl was pinned via dnf versionlock immediately after capturing its baseline version, the lock was verified in both the versionlock list and the persisted config file, and a full dry-run update transaction covering many other packages explicitly excluded curl. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly for node1: a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 646e5f74..., systemctl is-system-running=running) was captured, the reboot was acknowledged via systemd-run before disconnection, a new boot_id (b0ab8d16...) was observed after reconnection, and post-restart state showed curl still installed at the locked version with the versionlock entry intact and system health running. The fixed before-prepare/after-executor snapshots corroborate the same boot_id transition and show no failed services or unexplained residue.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so the restart protocol's cross-node consistency could not be assessed beyond a single node.

The verification that a system update would leave curl untouched relies on a dry-run (--assumeno) rather than an actual completed update; this is a reasonable and non-destructive way to demonstrate the effect without performing a full risky package update, but it is not a live post-update observation of a real upgrade transaction.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 19 executor commands chronologically. Every state-changing command maps clearly to a task purpose: installing the versionlock plugin (cmd-0dd5b4a28dc7434f failed with a GPG parsing error and was immediately retried successfully as cmd-85c670e8857443f2, a legitimate corrective retry rather than an unnecessary mutation), applying the versionlock (cmd-bdb20c5d62d64600), and the mandated provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-32a2d4f5a3984ec7 scheduling reboot via systemd-run, followed by polling commands cmd-3f97bfa0794a41b2/cmd-09632d3ecaeb420b/cmd-b0ea6becf6244159 which returned -1/timeout as expected transient disconnection during reboot, not failures). No unbounded, destructive, or unexplained mutations were found; no residue beyond expected reboot-generated systemd-private temp directories, which is normal reboot behavior and not executor-caused clutter.
